label: eq:evenoperatorintegral
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Even-value differential-operator integral

label: eq:evenkernel
title: Proof
body_md:
For a single positive ordinate $\gamma$, write
\[
f_\gamma(x)=\log\!\left(1+\frac{x^2}{\gamma^2}\right).
\]
With $t=x^2/\gamma^2$, one has $\mathcal E=2t\,\,\mathrm d/\,\mathrm d t$.  A direct induction
therefore gives
\begin{equation}
\mathscr D_k f_\gamma(x)
=(-1)^k2^{k+1}k!\,
\frac{x^{2k+2}}{(\gamma^2+x^2)^{k+1}}.
\label{eq:evenkernel}
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\[
(-1)^k\frac{\mathscr D_k f_\gamma(x)}{x^{2k+1}}
=2^{k+1}k!\frac{x}{(\gamma^2+x^2)^{k+1}},
\]
which is non-negative.  Since
\(
L(x)=\sum_{\gamma>0}f_\gamma(x)
\), Tonelli's theorem permits the sum over $\gamma$ to be interchanged
with the integral, and
\[
\int_0^\infty\frac{x}{(\gamma^2+x^2)^{k+1}}\,\,\mathrm d x
=\frac{1}{2k\,\gamma^{2k}}.
\]
It follows that
\[
\int_{0}^{\infty}
\frac{\mathscr D_kL(x)}{x^{2k+1}}\,\,\mathrm d x
=(-1)^k2^k(k-1)!\,Z(2k),
\]
which proves \eqref{eq:evenoperatorintegral}.  The same calculation also
proves absolute convergence.  Near $x=0$, the operator $\mathscr D_k$ removes
the terms $x^2,x^4,\ldots,x^{2k}$, so the resulting integrand is $O(x)$;
at the upper endpoint, Tonelli's identity gives a finite total integral
because $Z(2k)<\infty$.

label: eq:remainderintegral
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Odd-value remainder integral

title: Proof
body_md:
For one ordinate $\gamma$, put $y=x/\gamma$ and define
\[
r_k(y)=\log(1+y^2)-\sum_{m=1}^{k}(-1)^{m+1}\frac{y^{2m}}{m}.
\]
A finite geometric sum gives
\[
r_k'(y)=\frac{2(-1)^k y^{2k+1}}{1+y^2}.
\]
The boundary terms vanish in an integration by parts, and hence
\[
\int_0^{\infty}\frac{r_k(y)}{y^{2k+2}}\,\,\mathrm d y
=\frac{1}{2k+1}\int_0^{\infty}\frac{r_k'(y)}{y^{2k+1}}\,\,\mathrm d y
=\frac{(-1)^k\pi}{2k+1}.
\]
Scaling by $x=\gamma y$ supplies the factor $\gamma^{-(2k+1)}$.  Moreover, $(-1)^kr_k(y)\geq0$ for $y\geq0$, so Tonelli's theorem justifies interchanging the sum over $\gamma$ with the integral.  Summing over all positive ordinates proves \eqref{eq:remainderintegral}.

body_md:
Set $t=x^2/\gamma^2$.  Then $\mathcal E=2t\,\,\mathrm d/\,\mathrm d t$ and
\[
\mathcal E f_\gamma=\frac{2t}{1+t}.
\]
An induction gives
\[
\prod_{j=1}^{k}\left(t\frac{\,\mathrm d}{\,\mathrm d t}-j\right)\frac{t}{1+t}
=(-1)^k k!\frac{t^{k+1}}{(1+t)^{k+1}},
\]
which is equivalent to \eqref{eq:Dkernel}.
